correctness.rationale: On each dyadic interval Parseval forces the binary subtree sum to solve s-s²/n=V measured from descendants, hence allows only original or complementary sums. Two distinct parent contrast orientations are simultaneously feasible exactly for a balanced nonzero parent contrast, with a complement-bijection of child choices. Induction yields 2^b fibers. A second weight induction gives b≤min(k,N-k), explicit separated pairs attain equality, and top-fiber equality forces all adjacent pairs mixed. Every binary input up to length 16 was checked by a standalone exact full census, including 65536 length-16 vectors, plus exact rational local Parseval tests. Exhaustive small tests are not used as an all-length proof.

originality.rationale: The full-text HTML proofs and hypotheses in arXiv:2302.08129 (intro and Theorem 3.3) and arXiv:1601.07579 (intro, Meyer-wavelet theorem) concern oversampled continuous-signal wavelet sign retrieval. They do not imply an exact binary nonredundant Haar-basis fiber cardinality, a per-Hamming-weight sharp extremum, or its unique maximal observation class. Actual mathematical-record and literature searches for binary Haar magnitudes, sign ambiguity and tree reconstruction identified related but noncovering Fourier/STFT and binary-word measurements. An unindexed hierarchical-data equivalent remains a historical priority risk.
residual_risks: Older work on dyadic hierarchical binary reconstruction, quantized wavelet coefficients, or coding theory may encode the same exact fiber count under different language.
Not all historical non-indexed papers and downstream sources were inspected; no claim of absolute historical uniqueness.
Finite exact tests support but do not replace the all-length proof.

value.rationale: The fiber exponent is a new sharply defined structural statistic of a natural complete, nonredundant multiscale orthobasis on quantized signals. Its exact measurement-preimage law, sharp exponent at every Hamming weight, complete singleton classification and unique largest ambiguity fiber answer direct reconstruction-design questions; these are not mere deductions from known generic failure of real orthobasis phase retrieval. The phenomenon scales exponentially in signal length and the theorem gives an exact O(N) diagnostic.
